chunks: From him, from Ahmad, from al-Barqi, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon him), that he used to say:

"Whoever dies and with him is capital for mu'darabah (profit-sharing partnership), he said: 'If he named it specifically before his death, saying: This is for so-and-so, then it is for him; and if he died and did not mention it, then it is the example/share of the creditors.'"
ai.seo_question: What happens to partnership capital if the investor dies without a specific will?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq clarifies the status of *mu'darabah* capital upon the investor's death, distinguishing between specific bequest (*takhassus*) and general estate (*aswata al-ghurama'*). In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights that if the partner is not explicitly named, the capital reverts to the pool of creditors rather than being treated as a general legacy, ensuring priority in debt settlement. This ruling underscores the precision required in commercial contracts to preserve the rights of stakeholders in inheritance scenarios.
